title: Simply Savage v0.4
author: Tony P.
desc:
SIMPLY SAVAGE

This my first program I have written and published. It is a culmination of my experience, research, and education on health and fitness, in particular, bodybuilding. Thank you for taking the time to review the program even if you do not decide to try it!

Who is this program for?


- People with at least 1+ year(s) experience in the gym
- Natural lifters
- Those on a bulk or maintaining
- Lifters interested in an easy program to follow and repeat


What are the program's principles?


Longevity - the program blends a combination of less compromising exercises (when done correctly) and functional work to ensure we stay in the gym longer.

Simplicity - no weird exercises, nothing nobody has never seen, progression is simple to follow.

Coverage - the program is intended to cover all muscle groups including ones that are often neglected (traps, lower back, gait, rotation, etc.).

Variation - no repeat exercises on a day to day basis, a mix of rep ranges, and intensity. Exercises are selected based on effectiveness and safety.

Modularity - workouts are structured to have 3 separate groups, should you find yourself short on time or low on energy, you can swap or skip exercises when needed.


Program's specifics:

Structure - there are 3 groups of exercises, main, secondary, and functional. The main group we try to progress on a week to week basis. The secondary group is to get additional work on certain muscle groups. Functional group are exercises targeting often missed muscles groups/movements. The main goal is completing the main group on a daily basis.

Progression - Each week is a different goal. Week 1 we set our baseline to measure progression, week 2 we increase our sets, week 3 we increase reps, week 4 we max out, week 5 we de-load.

Please try and follow the guidelines in the workout. It is not perfect but if followed, you should see progression in both muscle and strength. 

Main lifts in the program are the ones we are trying to progress in. For our main lifts there will be a “top set” where we will work harder than the others. RPE is the same as RIR (reps in reserve) for this program. So an RPE 8 means you leave 2 reps in reserve as far as fatigue goes. 

Schedule - there are 5 days in the program, 3 "power" days, and 2 "hypertrophy" days. The difference between them is rep ranges, intensity, and form. An example week of this program might look like this:

Sunday - Off
Monday - Push Power
Tuesday - Pull Power
Wednesday - Legs Power
Thursday - Off
Friday - Upper Hypertrophy
Saturday - Lower Hypertrophy

ex.note: Main lift. Chest and shoulders. 2 warmup sets. The way this works for main lifts is if there is warmup sets, do them. Then start with your top set and lower the weight for subsequent sets.
Main lift. Triceps. Here you do 1 warmup set, then your top set, lower the weight then set 2. Remember RPE is RIR (RPE 8 means 2 RIR).
Main lift. Chest and triceps. Jump right into the top set. Bang out 8 where you feel you could do 2 more, then bang out 8 where you feel you could do 3 more. Then 8 where you could do 4+ more.
Secondary lift. Shoulders. No cheating, do these strict. For secondary work, there is no top set. Just maintain intensity and move the weight down as you do more sets (or maintain weight).
Secondary lift. Triceps. No top set, just do 3 sets there you feel you can do just about 3 left each set.
Functional lift. Shoulders. Here is where functional work comes into play. Longevity is the name of the game. Try to do these with more external rotation. Show our shoulders some love.
Functional lift. Gait. Gait work is an under appreciated exercise type. I do these with a plate doing a pinch grip. Congrats on completing day 1!
Main lift. Lats and biceps. Let your lats stretch at the top. For this lift, do 2 warmup sets, 1 top set, 2 additional working sets.
Main lift. Biceps. Keep your elbows as far back as you can. 1 warmup set, 1 top set, 1 working set. You should get the gist by now.
Main lift. Lats. Try to pinch your mid traps, drive your elbows back and into your lats. No warmup, right into top set. From here on out you are on your own.
Secondary lift. Traps. You can do these barbell or smith machine. Shoulders to ears and pause slightly at the top of each rep. This workout will make your mom think you are on roids.
Secondary lift. Biceps. Try to let the biceps stretch as much as you can but be careful. Nothing like a double bicep day to feel like a god.
Functional lift. Lower back. Try to curl your body more so than keeping a flat back. Be careful on these and do them slow, underrated exercise to injury prevention.
Functional lift. Abs. Do these to pull all the blood out of our lower back if this killer pull day. Day 2 DONE!
Secondary lift. Glutes and hamstrings. Taught by John Meadows (RIP), always start leg day with the hammies.
Main lift. Legs. A** to grass depth and keep the form crisp. If you need to do just the bar, so be it. Form over everything else for this exercise.
Main lift. Legs. Do either stationary or walking (if stationary, reset each rep). Man-maker exercise, go hard.
Secondary lift. Quads. Flex, squeeze and hold at the top of each rep. Finish strong.

Secondary lift. Calves. Flex at the top, hold, deep stretch at the bottom, hold. 
End the day strong.
Functional lift. Abs. This exercise is done incorrectly by too many people. Please watch a video on the proper form. Done with our first hell day.
Main lift. Chest. Really squeeze the pecs together. For hypertrophy days, focus on controlling the eccentric and squeezing the contraction of each exercise. These will fix your man boobs.
Main lift. Lats & biceps. Drive the elbows deep into your lat. For these, hold at the bottom, then control the stretch up. We want the wings.
Main lift. Shoulders and traps. Do these with the Jeff Nippard form. Hold the raise, control on the way down. You might hate him, but he has good form on these.
Secondary lift. Biceps. Do these both arms at a time and face away from the cable machine. Hold the curl, control on way down. Let those biceps stretch.
Secondary lift. Triceps. Do the form that gets the most pump for you. Hold the contraction, control down. Goated tricep exercise.
Functional lift. Rotation. Be careful with these. Do lightweight and focus on the form 100%, not the weight or speed.
Secondary lift. Glutes and hamstrings. Hold at the top, control down. Always warm up the lower body with hamstring work. Always.
Main lift. Legs. Do these deficit, control 3secs down, hold at bottom for 2secs. Genuinely sorry for these, I usually can't walk after them.
Main lift. Glutes & hamstrings. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top and pause, control down. Time to build dat a**.
Secondary lift. Lower back/posterior chain. Do these seated holding a dumbbell between your legs. Gotta keep the low back strong.
Secondary lift. Calves. Flex at the top and hold, deep stretch at the bottom and hold. Nice 3 piece of our favorite muscle groups. Go hard if you want big calves.
Functional lift. Abs. Do each side. Highly underrated ab exercise, arguably my favorite.
Main lift. Chest and shoulders. Stop just before you touch your chest to save your rotator cuff. Start the week off with some pain adding a set to our main lifts. Welcome to week 2.
